messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate detected on smart-routing service (route-policy:v3). 5xx rate from API gateway -> smart-router up 18% over baseline in last 60s. Auto-escalating to on-call.
oncall-frontend: Got the pager, looking. Seeing a spike of 502/504s from /v1/generate. Marking as P1. Paging infra + runtime.
oncall-infra: I'm in. Throwing up quick dashboard: regional egress for eu-west-1 shows sudden increase in traffic to model-variant 'llama2-7b-q8' which is not available in that region — router is failing over to us-west-2. Latency and errors spike when failover occurs.
eng-runtime: Joining. Noted: smart-router policy 'prefer-lowcost' was updated ~10m ago (deploy-bot shows a canary). Policy maps requests to preferred variant family, but the mapping includes 'llama2-7b-q8' for eu-west-1 - we never provisioned that variant there. Fallback logic should pick compatible variant in-region but instead it's trying cross-region and simultaneously triggering request retries.
oncall-frontend: Client-side retry rate has also increased. I'm seeing a pattern: client retries (3x) + router failover -> duplicate hits to fallback region. That looks like an amplification loop.
sre-lead: Can we get the deploy details and the policy diff? @deploy-bot show me the rollout.
deploy-bot: Rollout summary: route-policy:v3 applied 2026-02-18T21:12:03Z by product-ops. Canary 10% -> 100% completed at 2026-02-18T21:18:45Z. Diff snippet:
```
- eu-west-1: prefer=redwood-llama2-7b (cpu)
+ eu-west-1: prefer=llama2-7b-q8 (gpu-optimized)
```
eng-runtime: That's the change. There is no gpu-optimized q8 build in eu-west-1; normally the router should fall back to the cpu-compatible redwood-llama2-7b in-region, but a matching rule uses variant family instead of capability set. Edge case: router thinks 'llama2-7b-q8' is compatible with 'llama2-7b' and attempts remote fetch.
oncall-infra: We have concurrent retries from clients configured for short retry windows: many SDKs are doing immediate retries with jitter=low. Combined with router failover (which triggers synchronous failover attempts), requests to us-west-2 doubled in a 30s window.
customer-success: Which customers are impacted? Any enterprise customers on Dedicated? We need talking points.
eng-runtime: Early telemetry: 1) 35% of requests from eu region got a cross-region hop after policy change. 2) 40% of those generated duplicate requests due to client retry loops. 3) Errors are mostly 502/504 from our proxy timeouts at the fallback region under load. Impact window started ~2026-02-18T21:19Z.
oncall-frontend: I'm going to rate-limit ingress to the smart-router for eu-west-1 to reduce fanout. Pushing a temporary throttle rule now: `policy: ingress-throttle eu-west-1 30rps`.
eng-runtime: Good. Also recommend disabling route-policy:v3 rollout (rollback to previous mapping) while we triage. @product-ops can you rollback?
product-ops: Rolling back now. Initiating rollback of route-policy:v3 to v2 mapping. Can confirm canary cancellation.
deploy-bot: Rollback started at 2026-02-18T21:24:12Z. Canary stopped. Full rollback completed at 2026-02-18T21:26:40Z.
oncall-infra: After rollback, cross-region hops dropped ~88% and error rate is decreasing but still elevated due to queued retries. We need to drain duplicate in-flight requests and avoid new retries. Can we put a server-side de-dup window for recently seen request-ids?
eng-runtime: We can short-circuit duplicate requests server-side if the SDK includes `client-request-id`. Short-term: add a request dedupe cache (100s TTL) for edge proxy to drop identical in-flight requests for same id. Patching now.
eng-runtime: Patching edge-proxy: config diff:
```
edge.proxy.dedupe.enabled = true
edge.proxy.dedupe.ttl = 15s
edge.proxy.dedupe.max_entries = 10000
```
oncall-frontend: Dedupe patch applied to eu-west-1 edge. I also bumped backoff recommended header for SDKs: `Retry-After: 120` to force clients to back off.
sre-lead: Good. Let's document mitigation steps in the incident channel and start handoff. @customer-success prepare customer comms: short note, impacted endpoints, ETA for resolution.
customer-success: Drafting message: "We detected increased errors on text generation endpoints for EU customers between 21:19-21:30 UTC due to a routing policy misconfiguration. Mitigations in place; service restored for most traffic. We'll follow up with postmortem." Will attach affected org list once infra confirms.
oncall-infra: Infra note: we also observed a small subset of Dedicated customers pinned to specific variants that experienced failed in-region mapping. Coordinating with sales/CS for those orgs.
eng-runtime: Temporary mitigation summary: 1) rollback policy -> reduced cross-region failover; 2) ingress throttle -> limited new load; 3) dedupe cache -> dropped duplicate inflight retries; 4) advised SDK update for exponential backoff. Latency and error rates trending back to baseline.
product-ops: Post-rollout action: revert change in route-policy staging test harness; add integration test that fails if policy maps to variant not present in region. Also add an automated validation step in rollout pipeline.
sre-lead: For follow-up (owner assignments): eng-runtime -> write router invariant tests (owner: @eng-runtime), infra -> add dedupe to runbook (owner: @oncall-infra), product-ops -> add gating to deploy pipeline (owner: @product-ops), customer-success -> send out final customer impact note (owner: @customer-success). We'll hold postmortem 2026-02-19 16:00 UTC.
oncall-frontend: Final check: error rate back to within 5% of baseline as of 21:51 UTC. Closing pager. If anything regresses, reopen.
incident-bot: Incident acknowledged as resolved by oncall-frontend at 2026-02-18T21:51:30Z. Incident #INC-2026-0218-79 closed. Postmortem scheduled.
sre-lead: Thanks everyone. Quick note for postmortem: investigate why router's compatibility matcher allowed a gpu-only variant label to be selected for eu-west-1. Also evaluate client-side default retry settings; consider adding server-side global rate limit for failover hops to prevent amplification.
